_note: Generated by scripts/gen-plainflags-tools.js from the real plain-flags relay — do not edit. plainflags-stub.py answers initialize and tools/list from it; test/plainflags-stub-drift.test.js keeps it current.

initialize.instructions: PLAIN-FLAGS relay: a separate, unseeded browser profile for Cloudflare walls (cf-challenge skill) — a fixed tool list, no saved logins, known accounts' logins refused unless on the sign-in list. Call relay_status for details.

tools.name: content_get-as-html
tools.description:
Gets the HTML content of the current page. 
By default, all <script> tags are removed from the output unless "removeScripts" is explicitly set to "false".

selector.description: Selector or ref; omit for full document.

output.description: The requested HTML content of the page.

tools.name: content_get-as-text
tools.description: Gets the visible text content of the current page.

selector.description: Limit text to this container; omit for full page.

output.description: The requested text content of the page.

tools.name: content_take-screenshot
tools.description:
Takes a screenshot of the current page or a specific element.
Do NOT use for page structure—use ARIA/AX snapshots instead.
Use only for visual verification (design check, visual bug, contrast, layout).
Screenshot is saved to disk; use includeBase64 only when the file cannot be read from the returned path (e.g. remote, container).

filePath.description: Full path of the saved screenshot file.

image.description: Image data included only when "includeBase64" input parameter is set to true.

annotations.description: When annotate is true, list of refs and bounding boxes. When selector is set: only annotations overlapping the element, box relative to that element. When fullPage is true: box is document-relative (matches the full-page image). Otherwise: viewport-relative.

tools.name: interaction_click
tools.description: Clicks an element. Accepts selector or ref (e.g. e1, @e1). Set waitForNavigation: true when the click opens a new page — waits for navigation then for network idle so snapshot/screenshot see full content.

selector.description: CSS selector or ref from a11y snapshot (e.g. e1, @e1).

waitForNavigation.description: Wait for navigation triggered by click (parallel with click). Use when click opens a new page.

waitForTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for navigation and for network idle wait (ms). Only when waitForNavigation is true. Default 30000.

allowPinnedPage.description: Relay-only. Run even though tabs_select / tabs_new could not point upstream's tab at the selected one (the relay then refuses this tool and says why). Acts on upstream's tab, not the selected one.

tools.name: interaction_fill
tools.description: Fills out an input field. Accepts a CSS selector or a ref from the last ARIA snapshot (e.g. e1, @e1).

selector.description: CSS selector or ref from a11y snapshot for the input.

tools.name: interaction_hover
tools.description: Hovers an element on the page. Accepts a CSS selector or a ref from the last ARIA snapshot (e.g. e1, @e1).

selector.description: CSS selector or ref from a11y snapshot.

allowPinnedPage.description: Relay-only. Run even though tabs_select / tabs_new could not point upstream's tab at the selected one (the relay then refuses this tool and says why). Acts on upstream's tab, not the selected one.

tools.name: interaction_press-key
tools.description:
Presses a keyboard key with optional "hold" and auto-repeat behavior.

Key facts:
- keyboard.press(key, { delay }) does NOT trigger OS-style auto-repeat.
- Some UI behaviors (especially scrolling) require repeated keydown events.
- Use repeat=true + holdMs to approximate real keyboard holding.

Execution logic:
- If selector is provided, the element is focused first.
- If holdMs is omitted or repeat=false:
  → a single keyboard.press() is executed.
- If holdMs is provided AND repeat=true:
  → keyboard.press() is called repeatedly until holdMs elapses.

selector.description: Focus this element first; omit for page focus.

repeat.description: Repeat key while holdMs (e.g. for scroll).

tools.name: interaction_select
tools.description: Select an option in a dropdown. Accepts a CSS selector or a ref from the last ARIA snapshot (e.g. e1, @e1).

selector.description: CSS selector or ref from a11y snapshot for the dropdown.

allowPinnedPage.description: Relay-only. Run even though tabs_select / tabs_new could not point upstream's tab at the selected one (the relay then refuses this tool and says why). Acts on upstream's tab, not the selected one.

tools.name: interaction_scroll
tools.description:
Scrolls the page viewport or a specific scrollable element.

Modes:
- 'by': Scrolls by a relative delta (dx/dy) from the current scroll position.
- 'to': Scrolls to an absolute scroll position (x/y).
- 'top': Scrolls to the very top.
- 'bottom': Scrolls to the very bottom.
- 'left': Scrolls to the far left.
- 'right': Scrolls to the far right.

Use this tool to:
- Reveal content below the fold
- Jump to the top/bottom without knowing exact positions
- Bring elements into view before clicking
- Inspect lazy-loaded content that appears on scroll

selector.description: Scrollable container: ref (e.g. from latest <a11y_take-aria-snapshot>), getBy… expression, or CSS. Omit for viewport.

allowPinnedPage.description: Relay-only. Run even though tabs_select / tabs_new could not point upstream's tab at the selected one (the relay then refuses this tool and says why). Acts on upstream's tab, not the selected one.

selector.description: The selector of the scroll container if provided; otherwise null (document viewport).

before.description: Scroll metrics before the scroll action.

after.description: Scroll metrics after the scroll action.

canScrollX.description: Whether horizontal scrolling is possible (scrollWidth > clientWidth).

canScrollY.description: Whether vertical scrolling is possible (scrollHeight > clientHeight).

isAtLeft.description: Whether the scroll position is at the far left.

isAtRight.description: Whether the scroll position is at the far right.

isAtTop.description: Whether the scroll position is at the very top.

isAtBottom.description: Whether the scroll position is at the very bottom.

tools.name: navigation_go-back-or-forward
tools.description:
Navigates to the previous or next page in history.
- `direction: "back"` — previous page in history.
- `direction: "forward"` — next page in history.

In case of multiple redirects, the navigation will resolve with the response of the last redirect.
If cannot go back/forward, returns empty response.

By default (includeSnapshot: true), an ARIA snapshot with refs is returned. Use `snapshotOptions` for `interactiveOnly` (default false) and `cursorInteractive` (default false), same as a11y_take-aria-snapshot.

When `includeScreenshot: true`, the screenshot is always saved to disk; `screenshotFilePath` is returned. By default `outputPath` is the OS temp dir and `name` is "screenshot" (same as content_take-screenshot). Use `screenshotOptions.includeBase64: true` only when the file cannot be read from the returned path (e.g. remote, container).

waitUntil.description: Playwright navigation lifecycle: when the main frame reaches this state. Does not use Playwright networkidle; use waitForNavigation for session network-idle after history navigation.

waitForNavigation.description: Wait for navigation then for network idle before snapshot/screenshot. Default true.

waitForTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for navigation and network idle wait (ms). Only when waitForNavigation is true. Default 30000.

includeScreenshot.description: Take a screenshot after navigation; saved to disk (default: OS temp dir). Use includeBase64 only when file cannot be read from path.

outputPath.description: Directory to save the screenshot. Default: OS temp dir.

name.description: Base name for the screenshot file. Default: "screenshot".

fullPage.description: Capture full scrollable page. Default: true.

annotate.description: Overlay ARIA ref labels on the screenshot. Default: true.

includeBase64.description: Include base64 image in response; use only when file cannot be read from path (e.g. remote, container).

screenshotOptions.description: Options when includeScreenshot is true. Same semantics as <content_take-screenshot> (outputPath/name default to tmp and "screenshot").

allowPinnedPage.description: Relay-only. Run even though tabs_select / tabs_new could not point upstream's tab at the selected one (the relay then refuses this tool and says why). Acts on upstream's tab, not the selected one.

url.description: Contains the URL of the navigated page.

status.description: Contains the status code of the navigated page (e.g., 200 for a success).

statusText.description: Contains the status text of the navigated page (e.g. usually an "OK" for a success).

ok.description: Contains a boolean stating whether the navigated page was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not.

screenshotFilePath.description: When includeScreenshot is true: full path of the saved screenshot file.

image.description: When includeScreenshot and screenshotOptions.includeBase64 are true: image sent as separate image content part.

tools.name: navigation_go-to
tools.description:
Navigates to the given URL.
**NOTE**: The tool either throws an error or returns a main resource response. 
The only exceptions are navigation to `about:blank` or navigation to the same URL with a different hash, 
which would succeed and return empty response.

**By default** (`includeSnapshot: true`), an ARIA snapshot with refs is taken after navigation and returned in `output` and `refs`; you can use refs (e1, e2, ...) in interaction tools without calling a11y_take-aria-snapshot separately. Use `snapshotOptions` for `interactiveOnly` (default false) and `cursorInteractive` (default false). Set `includeSnapshot: false` to get only url/status/ok.

When `includeScreenshot: true`, the screenshot is always saved to disk; `screenshotFilePath` is returned. By default `outputPath` is the OS temp dir and `name` is "screenshot" (same as content_take-screenshot). Use `screenshotOptions.includeBase64: true` only when the file cannot be read from the returned path (e.g. remote, container).

waitUntil.description: Playwright navigation lifecycle: when the main frame reaches this state. Does not use Playwright networkidle; use waitForNavigation for session network-idle after navigation.

waitForNavigation.description: Wait for navigation then for network idle before snapshot/screenshot. Default true.

waitForTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for navigation and network idle wait (ms). Only when waitForNavigation is true. Default 30000.

includeScreenshot.description: Take a screenshot after navigation; saved to disk (default: OS temp dir). Use includeBase64 only when file cannot be read from path.

outputPath.description: Directory to save the screenshot. Default: OS temp dir.

name.description: Base name for the screenshot file. Default: "screenshot".

fullPage.description: Capture full scrollable page. Default: true.

annotate.description: Overlay ARIA ref labels on the screenshot. Default: true.

includeBase64.description: Include base64 image in response; use only when file cannot be read from path (e.g. remote, container).

screenshotOptions.description: Options when includeScreenshot is true. Same semantics as <content_take-screenshot> (outputPath/name default to tmp and "screenshot").

allowPinnedPage.description: Relay-only. Run even though tabs_select / tabs_new could not point upstream's tab at the selected one (the relay then refuses this tool and says why). Acts on upstream's tab, not the selected one.

url.description: Contains the URL of the navigated page.

status.description: Contains the status code of the navigated page (e.g., 200 for a success).

statusText.description: Contains the status text of the navigated page (e.g. usually an "OK" for a success).

ok.description: Contains a boolean stating whether the navigated page was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not.

screenshotFilePath.description: When includeScreenshot is true: full path of the saved screenshot file.

output.description: When includeSnapshot is true: page URL, title, and ARIA tree with refs.

refs.description: When includeSnapshot is true: map of ref id (e1, e2, ...) to role/name/selector for use in interaction tools.

image.description: When includeScreenshot and screenshotOptions.includeBase64 are true: image sent as separate image content part.

tools.name: o11y_get-console-messages
tools.description: Retrieves console messages/logs from the browser with filtering options.

type.description: Filter by level (this level or higher).

timestamp.description: Only messages at or after this Unix ms.

sequenceNumber.description: Incremental: only messages with sequence > this.

from.description: Keep from start or end when truncating.

location.description: Location of the console message in the resource.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch timestamp (in milliseconds) of the console message.

sequenceNumber.description:
A monotonically increasing sequence number assigned to each console message.
It reflects the order in which messages were captured and can be used by clients
to retrieve messages incrementally by requesting only those with a higher sequence
number than the last one received.

tools.name: o11y_get-http-requests
tools.description: Retrieves HTTP requests from the browser with filtering options.

timestamp.description: Only requests at or after this Unix ms.

sequenceNumber.description: Incremental: only requests with sequence > this.

from.description: Keep from start or end when truncating.

method.description: HTTP request method. Valid values are: GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,HEAD,OPTIONS

headers.description: HTTP request headers as key-value pairs. Present when includeRequestHeaders was true.

resourceType.description:
HTTP request resource type as it was perceived by the rendering engine. 
Valid values are: document,stylesheet,image,media,font,script,texttrack,xhr,fetch,eventsource,websocket,manifest,other,ping,prefetch,signedexchange,cspviolationreport,preflight,fedcm

failure.description: Error message of the HTTP request if failed.

duration.description: HTTP request duration in milliseconds. "-1" if not available (no response).

headers.description: HTTP response headers. Present when includeResponseHeaders was true.

body.description: HTTP response body if available. Present when includeResponseBody was true.

ok.description:
Flag to represent whether the HTTP request successful or failed. 
An HTTP request is considered successful only if its status code is 2XX.
Otherwise (non-2XX status code or no response at all because of timeout, network failure, etc ...) it is considered as failed.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch timestamp (in milliseconds) of the HTTP request.

sequenceNumber.description:
A monotonically increasing sequence number assigned to each HTTP request.
It reflects the order in which requests were captured and can be used by clients
to retrieve requests incrementally by requesting only those with a higher sequence
number than the last one received.

tools.name: sync_wait-for-network-idle
tools.description:
Waits until the page is network-idle: in-flight requests <= maxConnections for at least idleTimeMs (server-side tracking, no page globals).
Use before SPAs, screenshots, or AX snapshots for stable results. With long-polling, increase maxConnections or use shorter idleTimeMs.

idleTimeMs.description: Network must stay idle for this many ms to resolve.

waitedMs.description: Total time waited until the network became idle or the tool timed out (milliseconds).

maxConnections.description: Idle threshold used: in-flight requests must be <= this value.

pollIntervalMs.description: Polling interval used to sample the in-flight request count (milliseconds).

finalInFlightRequests.description: The last observed number of in-flight requests at the moment the tool returned.

observedIdleMs.description: How long the in-flight request count stayed <= maxConnections right before returning (milliseconds).

tools.name: tabs_list
tools.description: List all open pages (tabs) in the relay's browser context with index, URL, and title. The `active: true` field marks the page tracked by tabs_new/tabs_select (this is what own-tools target by default).

tools.name: tabs_new
tools.description: Open a tab in the relay's browser context, optionally navigating to a URL. REUSES an existing tab when one is already open on the same host (keeps the tab strip lean) — pass forceNew:true if you genuinely need a second tab on that host. Tracks the resulting tab as the active page for subsequent own-tool calls.

forceNew.description: Always create a fresh tab, even when one is already open on the same host.

waitUntil.description: Playwright navigation lifecycle to wait for. Default 'load'. Use 'networkidle' for SPA-heavy sites.

allowPinnedPage.description: Only when the relay reported UPSTREAM DESYNC and the page in upstream's tab is one YOU put there: lets the relay reuse and navigate that tab. Never when the user may be using it.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait for the navigation in ms. Default 30s.

tools.name: tabs_select
tools.description: Select a tab (the active page for subsequent tools) by its index. It is raised on screen only when this relay's Brave is already the front app, so the user's focus is never taken.

allowPinnedPage.description: Only when the relay reported UPSTREAM DESYNC and the page in upstream's tab is one YOU put there: lets the relay navigate that tab to this one. Never when the user may be using it.

tools.name: tabs_close
tools.description: Close a tab/page by its index. Refuses to close the last remaining page. If you close the active page, the next-most-recent page becomes active automatically.

tools.name: dialog_handle
tools.description: Register a one-shot handler for the NEXT JavaScript dialog (alert/confirm/prompt) on the active page. Call this BEFORE the action that triggers the dialog. The handler resolves when the dialog appears and is auto-handled per the `action` parameter (accept by default, or dismiss). For prompts, set `promptText` to inject a value. If the page closes during the wait, the handler resolves immediately with isError + a `pageClosed: true` flag.

promptText.description: Text to type into a prompt dialog (only for action=accept)

timeoutMs.description: Max wait for the dialog to appear

tools.name: form_fill
tools.description: Fill multiple form fields on the active page in one call. Each field is { selector, value }. By default fills sequentially and stops on first failure (returning partial state). Set `continueOnError: true` to attempt every field regardless of failures. `timeoutMs` caps each field's wait (default 5000ms — Playwright's default 30000ms is too long when stacking many fields against a slow page). Useful when you have many text inputs and want one round-trip.

timeoutMs.description: Per-field timeout for the fill operation in ms (default 5000). Total time is roughly fields.length × timeoutMs in the worst case.

continueOnError.description: If true, attempt every field even after a failure. Result includes per-field ok/error. Default false (fail-fast).

tools.name: capture_xhr
tools.description: Record XHR/fetch responses observed by the active page during a navigation or fixed time window. Returns array of { url, status, method, contentType, headers, body? } per response. Useful for reverse-engineering site APIs while authenticated in the relay's browser session. When navigateToUrl is set, navTimeoutMs caps the navigation; durationMs is the total capture window (including the navigation time).

navigateToUrl.description: If provided, navigate the active page to this URL while capturing. Otherwise just capture for durationMs from now.

durationMs.description: Total capture window in ms (default 5s, max 5min). Also caps how long this tool blocks.

navTimeoutMs.description: Optional separate cap on the page.goto timeout when navigateToUrl is set. Defaults to min(durationMs, 30000). Set higher than the durationMs only if you want to fail navigation fast then keep listening.

waitUntil.description: Playwright navigation lifecycle when navigateToUrl is set. Default 'domcontentloaded' — 'networkidle' often hangs on chatty pages and burns the whole capture window.

urlFilter.description: Optional regex pattern (as a string) to filter URLs. Only matching responses are returned.

maxBodyBytes.description: Maximum body length per response (truncated if longer). Default 100KB.

maxResponses.description: Stop recording new responses after this many. Default 500 — prevents unbounded heap on chatty pages. When the cap is hit, `truncated: true` is set on the result and any responses past the cap are dropped.

maxTotalBytes.description: Aggregate cap on captured body bytes (default 50MB). Once exceeded, headers are still recorded but bodies are skipped with `bodyError: 'aggregate cap reached'`. Belt-and-suspenders against memory balloon when maxBodyBytes × maxResponses is set high.

tools.name: storage_clear-local
tools.description: Clear localStorage or sessionStorage on the active page's origin. Returns the count of keys that were removed. Use `keys` to remove only specific keys; omit it to clear the entire store.

keys.description: Optional. If provided, only these keys are removed. Omit to clear the entire store.

tools.name: challenge_detect
tools.description: Classify a Cloudflare wall ("Just a moment…", a Turnstile widget, a 429, an Access login) and say whose it is and where to route it — the cf-challenge skill's table, first match wins. Never clicks, never reloads. `lane` is REQUIRED (your `claude-ask whoami` lane). Shapes: {lane} on the loaded page → owner (highlevel|shopify|access|agency-test|agency|workersdev|vendor|none), kind, route, raw signals, and one line appended to the shared CF-WALL log when the page shows a wall (then do not append another by hand); {lane, origin, stage:"pre"} before navigating → that origin's Cloudflare cookie state (names only), remembered 10 min, nothing appended; {lane, origin, stage:"outcome"} after a plain-flags try (plain-flags relay only) → appends the outcome line. An eligible wall (HighLevel or vendor; interstitial or Turnstile; not a known account's login) keeps its route here and adds switchTo: browser-mcp-relay-plainflags (if this session has that server); in that relay it routes plainflags-try.

lane.description: Required. Your lane from `claude-ask whoami` (letters, digits, . _ / -).

origin.description: For stage pre/outcome: the site's origin, e.g. https://go.example.com.

stage.description: Omit to classify the loaded page.

tools.name: relay_status
tools.description: Browser profile status for this session: BASE (this project's saved logins) or CLONE (a copy whose logins are deleted at session end), who holds the base and since when, this session's Brave and CDP port, and the other clones in this project. Call it before any sign-in. Never launches a browser.

tools.name: challenge_click
tools.description: PLAIN-FLAGS RELAY ONLY. One click on the visible Cloudflare Turnstile checkbox of the active page — found through the frame tree (inside a form's cross-origin iframe or a shadow root), scrolled into view, clicked once with a CDP mouse sequence. ONE per host per 10 min across every plain-flags relay; a second is refused. No challenge frame → refused, nothing sent (widget: absent); an invisible-mode widget → refused (its token arrives on load: wait, then challenge_detect). Call it only when challenge_detect says clickBudget: 1.

lane.description: Your lane from `claude-ask whoami` (recorded with the click).

tools.name: cf_cookies_clear
tools.description: PLAIN-FLAGS RELAY ONLY. After a failed plain-flags try: clear the site's Cloudflare state. On a site with no account on the sign-in list (every site at start) it deletes EVERY cookie of the site's registrable domain (partitioned copies included) plus the challenges.cloudflare.com cookies partitioned under it; on a site whose account is listed, only cf_clearance, __cf_bm, _cfuvid and the challenge partition. Returns names and counts, never values.
